needs_result.text: Built a tool-calling LLM agent (LangChain, AWS Bedrock, Claude Haiku 4.5) for a multi-omics cancer research platform, with three tools for gene alias resolution, scoring-methodology explanation and dataset provenance.
Deployed the agent as a Docker container on AWS Lambda (Lambda Web Adapter) with ECR image pipelines, IAM execution roles and least-privilege policies.
Wrote the dissertation's AI-agent sections covering architecture, implementation and evaluation, including a documented hallucination-rate analysis and test-case outcomes.

Proposed the request flow: a user's text goes through the API and a customised prompt to the MCP server, where one LLM instance writes GraphQL queries against the client's Convex database and a second instance runs the statistical analysis before the result returns to the user.

Carried it into production with the client's engineering team: contributed to their production TypeScript/Node.js MCP server (OpenAI-based query generation, Convex), now in live use, and reviewed pull requests in the client's production repository alongside their CTO.
Built scikit-learn pipelines and LSTM/BiRNN/CNN models in TensorFlow/Keras, deployed as FastAPI services in Docker.
Built a production RAG and agentic retrieval system (Claude API, LangChain, LangGraph, ChromaDB) served through a FastAPI REST API in Docker on GCP Cloud Run.

Designed reproducible scikit-learn pipelines with feature engineering (temporal features, interaction terms, target encoding), model selection, cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning across classification and regression tasks.
Implemented offline-first data persistence (Isar) with background synchronisation in the Flutter FinTech app, keeping financial records available in low-connectivity conditions.

Shipped features in a production fintech (financial-services) application as part of a team: integrated Twelve Data (real-time market feeds) and Plaid (bank linking, transaction imports) via REST APIs, with SSL pinning and AWS Cognito SSO.

MCP server and stdio client combining web search with a GraphQL/PostgreSQL data layer, run against a local open-weight model (gpt-oss:20b) with CI across Python 3.9–3.11.

letter.closing: Could we take 20 minutes to talk about production, testing and CI/CD?
draft_body: At Graphcore you will build the software that validates Graphcore's machine learning stack, from frameworks to AI accelerator hardware. You will design production-quality test infrastructure that engineers can extend, maintain and rely on as Graphcore's ML software grows. You will architect scalable test frameworks and build CI/CD pipelines that run across simulators, emulators and physical hardware. This role gives you scope to shape software architecture and developer experience, not just add tests to existing systems.

I have a strong focus on testing, having applied systematic evaluation to verify complex pipelines and ensure correctness. In another project I combined omics and graph techniques to analyse large-scale biological datasets, processing 1,399 cell lines across 16,385 genes and achieving a clear separation between training and test performance. These experiences demonstrate my ability to construct reliable, reproducible test suites that surface issues early and provide clear evidence of numerical accuracy, directly aligning with Graphcore's need for rigorous ML stack validation. My work has been carried out in Python within Linux environments, reinforcing testability and maintainability. I designed evaluation frameworks that capture performance metrics across different hardware simulators, enabling developers to compare results consistently. Through iterative refinement I introduced automated regression checks that reduced manual review time and increased confidence in numerical results. These practices align with Graphcore's emphasis on clear evidence of numerical accuracy and performance across the stack and scalability in production.

I bring proven production expertise, having built end-to-end fintech APIs that operate reliably under heavy load and integrate smoothly with existing services. I also containerised critical workloads using Docker, deployed them on AWS Lambda and managed access through IAM policies, ensuring secure and scalable execution. My experience delivering production-grade software includes designing CI/CD pipelines that automate testing and deployment in Linux environments, reinforcing reliability across simulators and physical hardware. By applying these methods I have consistently reduced deployment friction and improved observability, supporting rapid iteration on complex systems. This background equips me to deliver the production-ready software Graphcore requires for its ML QA pipelines, enabling integration and automated testing across diverse hardware targets. I used Python scripts to orchestrate test runs and capture performance data, aligning with Graphcore's focus on scalable testing frameworks. Additionally I have contributed to tooling that streamlines CI/CD workflows, demonstrating my commitment to extensible solutions.
